Multivariate Imputation by Chained Equations (Iteration Step)

Source: R/mice.mids.R
mice.mids.Rd

Takes a mids object, performs maxit iterations and produces a new object of class "mids".

Usage

mice.mids(
  obj,
  newdata = NULL,
  maxit = 1,
  print = getOption("mice.print", getOption("mice.printFlag", TRUE)),
  future = !is.null(obj$future) || isTRUE(obj$parallel),
  ...,
  printFlag = print
)

Arguments

obj

An object of class mids, typically produces by a previous call to mice() or mice.mids()

newdata

An optional data.frame for which multiple imputations are generated according to the model in obj.

maxit

The number of additional Gibbs sampling iterations. The default is 1.

print

Logical. If TRUE (default), diagnostic information during the Gibbs sampling iterations is written to the console. See mice().

future

Logical. If TRUE, the chains are run as futures on the current future plan, as in mice(future = TRUE). The default continues in the mode in which obj was created. See Details.

...

Named arguments that are passed down to the univariate imputation functions.

printFlag

Legacy name of print, kept for backward compatibility. If given, it takes precedence over print.

Value

mice.mids returns an object of class "mids".

Details

This function enables the user to split up the computations of the Gibbs sampler into smaller parts. This is useful for the following reasons:

  • To add a few extra iteration to an existing solution.

  • If RAM memory is exhausted. Returning to prompt/session level may alleviate such problems.

  • To customize convergence statistics at specific points, e.g., after every maxit iterations to monitor convergence.

The imputation model itself is specified in the mice() function and cannot be changed in mice.mids(). The state of the random generator is saved with the mids object. This ensures that the imputations are reproducible.

By default, mice.mids() continues in the same way as the object was created: an object made with future = TRUE continues as futures on the current plan, and other objects continue with the classic sequential sampler. In both cases, the result is identical to that of a single call with all iterations. For an object made with future = TRUE, this works because the object stores the state of the random number stream of each chain (chainSeed).

It is possible to switch: future = TRUE continues a sequential object as futures, and future = FALSE continues a future object with the classic sampler, e.g. to see the iteration history or to debug an imputation method. The result is reproducible, but differs from a single call with all iterations, as the random numbers come from different streams.

See also

complete, mice, set.seed, mids

Examples

imp1 <- mice(nhanes, maxit = 1, seed = 123)
#> 
#>  iter imp variable
#>   1   1  bmi  hyp  chl
#>   1   2  bmi  hyp  chl
#>   1   3  bmi  hyp  chl
#>   1   4  bmi  hyp  chl
#>   1   5  bmi  hyp  chl
imp2 <- mice.mids(imp1)
#> 
#>  iter imp variable
#>   2   1  bmi  hyp  chl
#>   2   2  bmi  hyp  chl
#>   2   3  bmi  hyp  chl
#>   2   4  bmi  hyp  chl
#>   2   5  bmi  hyp  chl

# yields the same result as
imp <- mice(nhanes, maxit = 2, seed = 123)
#> 
#>  iter imp variable
#>   1   1  bmi  hyp  chl
#>   1   2  bmi  hyp  chl
#>   1   3  bmi  hyp  chl
#>   1   4  bmi  hyp  chl
#>   1   5  bmi  hyp  chl
#>   2   1  bmi  hyp  chl
#>   2   2  bmi  hyp  chl
#>   2   3  bmi  hyp  chl
#>   2   4  bmi  hyp  chl
#>   2   5  bmi  hyp  chl

# verification
identical(imp$imp, imp2$imp)
#> [1] TRUE

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# the same holds for chains run as futures
future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 2)
imp1 <- mice(nhanes, maxit = 1, seed = 123, future = TRUE)
imp2 <- mice.mids(imp1)
imp <- mice(nhanes, maxit = 2, seed = 123, future = TRUE)
identical(imp$imp, imp2$imp)
future::plan(future::sequential)
} # }
